description: Reproducible educational comparison of three pretrained CNNs for pediatric pneumonia classification. All descriptions below are generated from the stored numerical evidence. Raw predictions, checkpoints, executable Python and CSV tables accompany this JSON.

analysis_execution.description: Current analysis/export source hashes. Original launch-time hashes remain in source_files. Session-specific timing interpretation is generated without changing training or saved predictions.

pipeline.description: Check official dataset checksum and exact image duplicates; retain 4698/524/624 examples.
For each of three seeds, train each head for 2 epochs and partially fine-tune for 3; paired ResNet frozen control shares epoch-2 weights. Batch 16, AMP, fixed BN statistics.
Execute final checkpoints on the same test order in AMP and FP32; fixed threshold 0.5; save raw arrays.
Recompute per-run scores, sample SD and paired hierarchical bootstrap from saved predictions; never tune on test scores.
Time isolated forward calls and synthetic full-gradient steps with explicit warm-ups, synchronization and raw samples.
Write explanations with numerical results in this JSON, plus CSV, Markdown and PNG figures.

metric_definitions.auroc: Area under ROC: ranking of pneumonia above normal across thresholds; higher is better; chance is 0.5.
metric_definitions.ap: Average precision: stepwise precision-recall summary, not trapezoidal PR area; test prevalence baseline is 0.625.
metric_definitions.f1: Harmonic mean of pneumonia precision and recall at probability >= 0.5.
metric_definitions.precision: TP/(TP+FP): proportion of predicted pneumonia examples labeled pneumonia.
metric_definitions.sd: Sample standard deviation across three training seeds (ddof=1); not standard error or patient uncertainty.
metric_definitions.auroc_ci95: Exploratory percentile interval: 2000 paired seed-and-exact-image-cluster bootstrap draws.
metric_definitions.speedup: FP32 time divided by AMP time; below 1 means AMP was slower.
metric_definitions.peak_allocated_mib: Peak live tensor allocation in MiB; excludes unused reserved memory and driver/desktop allocations.

verification.description: All twelve checkpoint hashes, five-epoch histories, accepted splits and raw prediction-derived scores passed. This checks artifact consistency; checkpoint inference is checked separately by replay.

checkpoint_replay.description: All twelve models were strictly loaded and executed on all 624 real test images in AMP and FP32. These numbers compare replay against the same precision, not AMP against FP32.

dataset.description: PneumoniaMNIST+ actual 224 resolution; pediatric normal/pneumonia. Ten exact train/validation-overlap rows removed. Within-test duplicate images retained and grouped for bootstrap. No patient IDs; exact hash checks cannot prove patient independence.

comparison.label: ResNet-18 frozen
comparison.description: ResNet-18 frozen had mean test AUROC 0.969496 with seed SD 0.000877; F1 at 0.5 was 0.913090. These are means of three separate model scores, not an ensemble. This descriptive result does not establish superiority over another architecture.

comparison.label: ResNet-18 partial FT
comparison.description: ResNet-18 partial FT had mean test AUROC 0.988913 with seed SD 0.002105; F1 at 0.5 was 0.933518. These are means of three separate model scores, not an ensemble. This descriptive result does not establish superiority over another architecture.

paired_differences.comparison: ResNet-18 partial FT minus ResNet-18 frozen
paired_differences.description: Mean AUROC difference +0.019417; exploratory 95% interval [+0.011256, +0.029072] supports a positive within-benchmark difference. Three seeds and unknown patient dependence limit this inference; no multiplicity adjustment was applied.

paired_differences.comparison: ResNet-18 partial FT minus DenseNet-121 partial FT
paired_differences.description: Mean AUROC difference +0.003397; exploratory 95% interval [-0.002267, +0.009940] includes zero, so a reliable directional difference is not established. Three seeds and unknown patient dependence limit this inference; no multiplicity adjustment was applied.

paired_differences.description: Mean AUROC difference -0.003269; exploratory 95% interval [-0.008991, +0.002069] includes zero, so a reliable directional difference is not established. Three seeds and unknown patient dependence limit this inference; no multiplicity adjustment was applied.

limitations: Previously examined test set; no prospective blinded claim.
Single pediatric binary dataset; no adult multi-finding or clinical deployment conclusion.
Only three seeds; exact-image clusters do not capture unknown patient clusters.
Architecture comparisons are exploratory; inconclusive differences do not prove equivalence.
Hardware timings depend on device/software/session; fixed five-epoch training does not establish convergence.
Fresh runs are method reproductions; bitwise equality across hardware/software is not guaranteed.

bootstrap.description: Independent weighted positive-negative pair counting with half-credit for ties reproduces the original rank-sum resampling results within 1e-14.

statistics.throughput_limitation: Inference wall-throughput rates are recorded measurements. Original wall-duration denominators were not retained separately, so CUDA-event samples cannot independently reconstruct those denominators; case-selection/aggregation was checked against recorded rates. Synthetic step throughput is fully recomputed from saved synchronized wall step times.

project_details.Official project title, if already fixed: Comparitive Analysis and optimization of deep learning models on chest X-rays
project_details.Team member names: Kanav Singla, Utkarsh Dubey, Dushyant Bhardwaj.

verified_sources.title: ChestX-ray8: Hospital-scale Chest X-ray Database and Benchmarks on Weakly-Supervised Classification and Localization of Common Thorax Diseases
verified_sources.description: The original release describes report-derived labels for eight findings and 108,948 frontal images. Later ChestX-ray14 updates must be distinguished from that original release. Our pediatric binary dataset is different.

verified_sources.title: CheXNet: Radiologist-Level Pneumonia Detection on Chest X-Rays with Deep Learning
verified_sources.description: The reported radiologist comparison concerns pneumonia F1 on a specific test and annotation setup. It motivates a DenseNet baseline but does not establish universal clinical superiority or validate our models.

verified_sources.title: CheXpert: A Large Chest Radiograph Dataset with Uncertainty Labels and Expert Comparison
verified_sources.description: CheXpert provides report-derived observation labels with uncertainty and a focused expert comparison. We do not use that dataset or claim to reproduce its multi-finding evaluation.

verified_sources.title: Comparing different deep learning architectures for classification of chest radiographs
verified_sources.description: The authors compared sixteen architectures on CheXpert and a separate COVID-19 collection. Comparable shallower models motivate measuring resource costs; their dataset-specific scores are not our results.

verified_sources.title: CheXtransfer: Performance and Parameter Efficiency of ImageNet Models for Chest X-Ray Interpretation
verified_sources.description: The study evaluates transfer and truncation on CheXpert, reporting an average parameter-efficiency improvement without a statistically significant drop in its comparison. That does not prove equivalence; our fine-tuning control does not reproduce truncation.

verified_sources.title: MedMNIST v2 - A large-scale lightweight benchmark for 2D and 3D biomedical image classification
verified_sources.description: The 2023 paper describes the standardized MedMNIST v2 collection at 28-pixel resolution. Our actual 224-pixel MedMNIST+ file is identified separately by its release record and checksum, rather than being an upscaled copy of the paper's 28-pixel images.
